body.translated_text: Homage to the Great Compassionate One.

children.translated_text: The oceans of suffering in the three worlds have waves stirred by <s>karmas</s> (actions),
arising from wholesome, unwholesome, and other tainted [actions]. // Gs_1 //
Those [karmas] are born from passion, hatred, and the like—from the causes of <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions);
and the cause of the arising of those [afflictions] is likewise the [experience of] the desirable, undesirable, and so forth. // Gs_2 //
From the grasping of duality arise the graspings that apprehend objects,
and [the views of] permanence, pervasiveness, unity, and the like—these are the causes of all arising. // Gs_3 //
Therefore, a fortunate person who desires liberation for self and others
should avert [these causes] through the practice of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) and other excellent reasonings. // Gs_4 //
First, the apprehension of entities: one should regard all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), both external and internal,
as equal to space, which is devoid of all characteristics. // Gs_5 //
But having focused upon the entire world, overpowered by the grasping of things as real,
with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) as the prerequisite—[compassion] that dries up the ocean of suffering— // Gs_6 //
one should generate the jewel of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind), which brings about the welfare of self and others,
and the great waves of <s>bodhicaryā</s> (awakened conduct)—the <s>ṣaṭpāramitās</s> (six perfections) and the like. // Gs_7 //
Through the yoga of meditative absorption and its aftermath, one should proceed gradually through the <s>pañcamārga</s> (five paths),

children.text: dvividhāvaraṇaṃ chittvā dvau saṃbhārau prapūrya ca // Gs_8 //
children.translated_text: cutting through the two obscurations (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) and completing the two accumulations (<s>saṃbhāra</s>). // Gs_8 //
The fruit of the <s>trikāya</s> (three bodies [of a Buddha]) is to be attained. And the characteristic of attaining the <s>trikāya</s> is:
from emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) like space, and from the cloud of effortless compassion (<s>anābhogakaruṇā</s>), // Gs_9 //
ever moistening the three realms (<s>tridhātu</s>) with streams of nectar of the two [form and formless] bodies (<s>dvikāya</s>),
from the excellent seeds of the field of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), one ripens the harvests of merit. // Gs_10 //
This <s>Garbhasaṅgraha</s> (Compendium of the Essence) is the heart of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
Because of the end-times, lifespans are short, diseases are many, and enjoyments are few; // Gs_11 //
because of bad causes, many obstacles, and inability to remain for long,
and because the [textual] tradition cannot be [maintained] without interruption, one should rely on a good spiritual friend (<s>sanmitra</s>). // Gs_12 //
With a mind of utmost vigor, earnestly mindful of the precipice [of saṃsāra],

children.text: saṅgṛhīto 'ñjasā garbho moktuṃ svaṃ ca paraṃ tathā // Gs_13 //
children.translated_text: this essence (<s>garbha</s>) has been directly compiled—to liberate oneself and others. // Gs_13 //
By the merit made from this with loving-kindness, may all unfortunate beings,

children.text: bodhicittamayā bhūtvā garbhaṃ gṛhṇantu cāñjasā // Gs_14 //
children.translated_text: having become filled with <s>bodhicitta</s>, directly grasp this essence! // Gs_14 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Garbhasaṅgraha</s> composed by the great <s>Ācārya Dīpaṅkaraśrījñāna</s> is completed.
